artists.biography:
Del Amitri were a Scottish alternative rock band, formed in Glasgow, Scotland in 1983. The band grew out of Justin Currie's Jordanhill College School band and came together after teenager Currie placed an advertisement in the window of a music store asking for people who could play to contact him. The band was formed with the original line-up of Currie (bass and vocals), Iain Harvie (lead guitar), Bryan Tolland (guitar) and Paul Tyagi (drums). Currie and Harvie were the only members of the band to remain present throughout its history. They were also the main songwriters of the group.

Despite having had several Top 10 albums in the UK, the group has never managed a Top 10 single in the UK Singles Chart, although they did achieve one Top 10 single, "Roll to Me", on the Billboard Hot 100 in the US.

perplexity.description:
Waking Hours is the second studio album by Scottish alternative rock band Del Amitri, originally released in July 1989 by A&M Records. The album marked a significant turning point in the band's career, establishing their signature sound characterized by melodic guitar-driven rock, introspective lyrics, and a blend of jangly pop sensibilities with a darker, more atmospheric edge. Recorded in Glasgow and London, the album features contributions from guitarist Mick Slaven and showcases the band's knack for crafting memorable hooks and emotionally resonant songwriting.

Musically, Waking Hours stands out for its balance of accessible rock anthems and nuanced, reflective tracks, setting it apart from the band's earlier, more experimental work. It was Del Amitri's commercial breakthrough, reaching number 6 on the UK Albums Chart and earning widespread critical acclaim for its cohesive songcraft and emotional depth. The album's success solidified Del Amitri's place in the late 1980s British rock scene and laid the foundation for their subsequent releases.
